input.text: Juyongguan is the Great Wall's front door to Beijing — the closest great mountain pass to the city, guarding the gorge through which every invader and every emperor once traveled. The pass today shows a grand Ming-dynasty fortress rebuilt in gleaming stone: twin gatehouses, looping walls hugging the valley, and the inscription that every visitor photographs — "The First Magnificent Pass Under Heaven." The true treasure is older: inside the fortress stands the Cloud Platform, a white-marble archway from the Yuan dynasty, thirteen forty-five. Walk through its tunnel and look up — the walls and ceiling are covered in thousands of carved Buddhas and inscriptions of sacred texts in six scripts: Chinese, Sanskrit, Tibetan, and more — a fourteenth-century monument to one empire's many languages. It's steeper than Badaling, quieter than Badaling, and under ninety minutes from the city. For a wall trip without the crowds, this is the insider's choice.
